feedback:
- Category: test
- Severity: high
- File: server/src/core/model-tier-config-reader.test.ts — the two linked-worktree tests (the test named “uses the main-worktree config rather than a divergent linked-worktree copy” and the test named “ignores inherited Git directory overrides when resolving a linked worktree”)
- Finding: Both tests call `git("worktree", "add", "-b", "linked-branch", linked)` where `linked` is a subdirectory of the main repository (`join(root, "linked")`). Git refuses to create a worktree inside the main worktree. The `execFileSync` call will throw, causing the test to fail and preventing the critical linked-worktree resolution behaviour from being exercised. This contradicts the spec’s confidence calibration that divergent linked-worktree config is empirically tested.
- Suggestion: Restructure the tests so the linked worktree is created in a separate temp directory outside the main worktree, then write a divergent `shipwright_model_config.json` there, and assert that the reader still resolves to the main-root copy. This will make the tests executable and provide the promised coverage.

Overall assessment: The implementation satisfies the acceptance criteria and is correctly wired end-to-end, but the linked-worktree safety net is broken – the test itself cannot run. Fix the test so the suite actually exercises the main-worktree resolution, then ship.
